## Caching in Computer Systems

Caching is one of the most important ideas in computer systems. It is a technique used to store copies of frequently accessed data in a faster, more accessible location so that future requests can be served more quickly. Although the basic idea is simple, caching appears throughout computing: in processors, operating systems, databases, web browsers, content delivery networks, and distributed systems. Its central purpose is to reduce latency, improve throughput, and lower the cost of accessing expensive resources.

At its core, caching exploits a fundamental property of computer programs: locality of reference. Programs do not access all data uniformly. Instead, they tend to access certain data repeatedly or access data that is close to what was accessed recently. C
